guard_streams.source: Bulletin: BDUK Delivery Performance, annual: April 2025 to March 2026
guard_streams.write_limit: Annual subsidy-delivery statistics are aggregate programme outputs and cannot establish current serviceability or measured speed for a selected parcel without an exact premises-level join.

facts.detail: The annual official-statistics bulletin was published on 11 June 2026.
The release covers subsidised gigabit-capable delivery from 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.
BDUK estimated 192,570 premises delivered in 2025/26.
Annual delivery increased by 42,280 premises, or 28 percent, compared with the previous financial year.
The estimated cumulative total since BDUK gigabit programmes began reached 1,418,410 premises.
GIS contracts accounted for 72 percent, or 139,490 premises, of 2025/26 delivery.
Voucher schemes accounted for 16 percent, or 30,530 premises.
Rural areas represented 90 percent, or 173,190 premises, of annual delivery.
Residential properties represented 90 percent, or 173,270 premises, of annual delivery.
The release used BDUK management information, NSUL, NSPL, Ofcom Spring 2026 Connected Nations, AddressBase Premium and national postcode sources.

guard_streams.source: Quality and Methodology Information for BDUK Delivery Performance, annual: April 2025 to March 2026
guard_streams.write_limit: The QMI explains methods, estimates, source systems and limitations; it is not itself a current parcel-coverage dataset.

facts.detail: The annual 2025/26 QMI was published on 11 June 2026.
The report documents data-quality characteristics and methods used to create the statistics.
It is intended to help users understand strengths and limitations of the data.
It supports decisions about suitable use and reducing data misuse.
The source stack includes ONS, NISRA, Scottish Government and AddressBase Premium geographic data.
BDUK uses Ofcom premises- and postcode-level data to estimate whether subsidised premises are in Ofcom's premises base.
The methodology uses the most recent Connected Nations dataset available.
Supplier UPRNs are validated and expected premises are filtered through BDUK's uncommercial-cost model.
A five percent attrition rate based on Ofcom data is applied in one voucher counting method.
An 18 percent attrition adjustment is used in the multiplier approach where expected-premises data is unavailable or poor.

guard_streams.source: Bulletin: BDUK delivery performance, quarterly: October 2025 to Dec 2025
guard_streams.write_limit: Quarterly official statistics report aggregate subsidy-attributable delivery and revised time series, not current selected-parcel orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: The bulletin covers delivery from 1 October to 31 December 2025.
BDUK estimated 56,000 premises delivered during the quarter.
The cumulative estimate reached 1,373,800 premises.
GIS accounted for 75 percent, or 41,830 premises, of quarterly delivery.
Vouchers accounted for 18 percent, or 10,150 premises.
Superfast and Hubs accounted for seven percent, or 4,050 premises.
Residential premises accounted for 90 percent, or 50,200 premises.
England accounted for 80 percent, or 45,100 premises.
The release is designated official statistics and produced under the Code of Practice for Statistics.
The source stack included BDUK management information, NSUL, NSPL, Connected Nations 2025 and AddressBase Premium.
